simple.meaning: אָבַק (ʼâbaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bedust , i.e. grapple.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 32:25. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָבַק (H79) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָבַק (ʼâbaq) / H79 is traced through Genesis 32:25, Genesis 32:26 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H79. abaq [ אָבַק ] verb denominative Niph`al wrestle (= get dusty , compare κόνις , κονίω , see also Str Pirke Aboth, 1, 4 רַגְלֵיהֶם בַּעֲפַר מִתְאַבֵּק = sit at their feet ; others, e.g. Di, compare חבק ). עִם וַיֵּאָבֵק Gen 32:25 ; Infinitive suffix עִם בְּהֵאָֽבְקוֺ 32:26 . אבר (compare Assyrian abâru , be firm , strong Dl W ).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from 80 ;

occurrences.englishText: When he saw that he didn’t prevail against him, the man touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained as he wrestled.
The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.”
